//lastChange: Pharmacy subdomains, second attempt (2026-09-08). The first used *.rxnaija.com with on-demand TLS and took the dashboard offline three times: that wildcard matches app.rxnaija.com, so Caddy served the DASHBOARD through the on-demand policy instead of the certificate it had held for months, and answered every handshake with tlsv1 alert internal error. Pharmacy subdomains worked throughout, which is why it survived three deploys. Neither allowlisting the dashboard in the ask endpoint nor giving it an explicit TLS connection policy helped — the failure is in which policy Caddy selects, not what it permits. Replaced with scripts/generate-caddy-sites.js, which writes one explicit site block per published address: no wildcard exists to capture a sibling. The 8 new tests cover the one genuinely dangerous part — those hostnames come from a column pharmacy owners control and are written into a Caddy config, where a brace or a newline is not a bad hostname but a new site block.
